public_rationale: Read plainly, the claim is that Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta, Oracle and others together held at least $200 billion of AI chips that were not installed, not powered or held in reserve in Q3 2026, up to the 2026-09-29 post date. Yahoo Finance, citing Business Insider on 2026-10-21, reports that Amazon takes ownership of NVIDIA GB300 racks before data centers or power are ready. An internal email projected about $5 billion of deliveries in August 2026 and about $3 billion a month after that. Amazon called staging hardware "best business practice." In November 2025, before the target period, Microsoft's CEO said he had chips in inventory that he could not plug in. He gave no dollar figure. In October 2026, after the post, Google's CEO said its compute is in use and capacity constrained. That is a company statement, not an inventory count. No item gives a combined dollar value of idle or reserve chips across these firms for Q3 2026. The evidence neither confirms nor rules out the $200 billion level.
limitations: The Amazon figures are projected deliveries from an internal email, reported secondhand, for one company. They do not show how much hardware was actually held unpowered, or for how long.
The Nadella quote is from November 2025, before the target period, and gives no dollar amount.
The Pichai statement is from after the post date and is not a measurement.
No evidence covers Meta, Oracle or the other unnamed firms.
The evidence does not separate chips held in reserve from normal staging before installation.

statement.excerpt: Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta, Oracle, and far too many other companies have been hoarding hundreds of billions of dollars of AI chips that they either (to quote Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella) can’t plug in or simply want to have in supply for reasons that I find tough to imagine.

from_speaker: "Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta, Oracle, and far too many other companies"
"hundreds of billions of dollars of AI chips"
"either ... can't plug in or simply want to have in supply"
our_interpretation: Plain reading: taken together, these firms hold at least $200 billion of AI chips that are bought but not installed or not powered, or are kept in reserve.
"Have been hoarding" describes an ongoing state at the post date. Target period: Q3 2026 through the post date (2026-07-01 to 2026-09-29), the latest period public reporting could cover.
Chips installed and running, even if lightly used, do not count.
criteria.support_condition: Credible disclosures or reporting showing that the named firms and others together hold at least about $200B of AI chips not installed, not powered, or held in reserve, around Q3 2026.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible measurement showing that the combined value of such idle or reserve AI chips at these firms is well below $200B in Q3 2026.
